title: Warmer Colours Only
tests: Tests interpreting 'warmer' as a colour-temperature adjustment rather than a scene or weather change.

faults.what: The colour treatment also increases saturation and contrast noticeably, making foreground trees and shoreline shadows darker and some fine detail harder to see.

judge.summary: The lake scene is visibly warmer with its composition and reflections preserved, though the colour treatment is somewhat heavy in saturation and shadow contrast.

must_haves.item: The image has a visibly warmer colour balance than the source.
must_haves.why: Clouds, mountain highlights and lake reflections have stronger yellow and golden tones.

must_haves.item: The same mountains, pine trees, clouds and lake remain in their original positions.
must_haves.why: The visible landmarks and cloud shapes match the source in placement and shape.

must_haves.item: The lake's reflections and surface details retain their original structure.
must_haves.why: Reflected mountains, clouds, trees and ripple patterns remain aligned with the source.

must_haves.item: No sun, sunset, extra clouds or other scene elements are added.
must_haves.why: No new scene elements are visible; the existing warm highlights have simply been intensified.

must_haves.item: Framing, geometry and image detail remain unchanged apart from colour.
must_haves.why: The crop, geometry and visible detail patterns match, with differences confined to tonal and colour treatment.
